_comment: Cell descriptor for layout/bin/compose-cell.py -- see layout/README.md
section 'Composing a gate' for the floorplan reasoning shared with every
other cell here, and layout/sampler_dff/README.md for this cell's own
result and open items (issue #27 step 5 / issue #22).
sampler_dff is design/sampler_core.spice's 22-device transmission-gate
master-slave DFF, composed entirely from the three leaf shapes issue #27
already established: layout/ro_buf/ (plain inverter), layout/sampler_tg/
(transmission gate), layout/sampler_nand2/ (rst_n-gated NAND2). Reading
the flat device list (design/sampler_core.spice's own .subckt sampler_dff)
as a signal-flow graph rather than a device list shows it is almost a
linear pipeline with two small local feedback loops, not a crossbar:
clk -> inv_clk -> clkb
d -> TG_D(clk/clkb) -> m -> NAND_M(m,rst_n) -> mb -> inv_mc -> mc
-> TG_FBM(clkb/clk) -> (feeds back into m)
mb -> TG_S(clkb/clk) -> s -> inv_q -> q -> NAND_S2(q,rst_n) -> qb
-> TG_FBS(clk/clkb) -> (feeds back into s)
(TG_FBM/TG_FBS run the OPPOSITE clk/clkb phase from their own stage's
input TG, the standard master-slave transparent-when-off-phase
structure -- confirmed against design/sampler_core.spice's own
Mtdp/Mtdn (clk/clkb), Mfmp/Mfmn (clkb/clk), Mtsp/Mtsn (clkb/clk),
Mfsp/Mfsn (clk/clkb) gate assignments.)
This is a placement-only first stage (issue #27/#22 increment N): nine
already-composed sibling cells (3x ro_buf, 4x sampler_tg, 2x
sampler_nand2) placed in signal-flow left-to-right order with generous
(3.0 um bbox-to-bbox) spacing, zero routing. Verified DRC-clean on its
own -- the same 'place' stage technique layout/ro_ring5/cell.json used
for the identical reason (prove the floorplan has no collisions before
attempting the harder net-by-net routing). See layout/sampler_dff/README.md
for the full port-coordinate derivation (every blocks[].cell.ports entry
below is either a value already proven by a prior increment -- e.g. the
sampler_nand2 en/a/y ports are IDENTICAL to layout/ro_ring5/cell.json's
own already-merged ro_nand2 reuse, since sampler_nand2's mpa/mpb/mnab
keep ro_nand2's own origins_um unchanged -- or independently derived from
each leaf's own klt gen/gen-compose response JSON and cross-checked
against a known-working example of the same orientation transform).
Routing (vdd/vss buses, rst_n fan-out, clk/clkb fan-out, and the six
data-path nets m/mb/mc/s/q/qb) is intentionally NOT attempted in this
increment -- see layout/sampler_dff/README.md's 'What remains' section.
This stage's own 'pins' list promotes every declared port of every block
under a unique '<id>_<port>' name so a later stage can address them.

stages.name: rst_n_stub
_comment: rst_n's two sampler_nand2 'a' pins (NAND_M/NAND_S2's rst_n input)
sit at local (4.98, 2.71) -- INSIDE sampler_nand2's own internal
met1 usage (a single via/pad blob spanning local x 4.455..5.045,
y 0.125..3.74, confirmed with klayout.db against sampler_nand2.gds:
this is the leaf cell's own internal 'y'-net via stack, not a port).
A metal2 via-drop landing directly on the pin (this cell's first
attempt) always shorts to that blob regardless of approach side --
gen-compose's own diagnostic ('self-net's drawn metal overlaps
block core's own drawn pad metal ... route to a layer_role with a
metal2/via stack instead') names exactly this. The fix used here: a
same-layer (li1/'metal' role, no via) stub FIRST, on each pin's OWN
native layer, carrying each 'a' pin EAST past the blob's east edge
(local x=5.045) before any metal2 transition. Both nand_m_a and
nand_s2_a use the same east-side escape (direction_deg 0, matching
sampler_nand2's own 'a' pin orientation, identical for both
instances since both are placed at orientation 'none').
The two stubs are the same in METHOD but NOT the same length. Each
tip is snapped to a round global x -- 14.0 for nand_m_a_ext, 44.9
for nand_s2_a_ext, which are also the final met3 bus's own two
endpoints (route_length_um 30.9 = 44.9 - 14.0) -- while the pins
themselves land wherever each instance's own placement origin puts
nand_s2. The two origins are 30.86um apart and the two tips 30.9um
apart, so the stubs run 0.57um (nand_m_a_stub) and 0.61um
(nand_s2_a_stub) -- exactly the route_length_um values
rst_n_stub.compose.response.json reports -- and the tips sit
0.425um / 0.465um east of their own instance's blob edge (global
13.575 and 44.435). Do not read the 0.04um difference as a
derivation asymmetry: neither stub is length-critical. What has to
clear the blob is the 0.42um-wide landing pad the NEXT stage's via
drops at the tip, and measured on the composed sampler_dff.gds
that pad spans x 13.79..14.21 against a blob edge at 13.575
(0.215um of met1-to-met1 space) and x 44.69..45.11 against 44.435
(0.255um) -- both clear, drc.json: 0 violations. An earlier,
shorter stub put that pad too close and drew the second
li1.space.1 violation this cell hit; 14.0 / 44.9 are simply the
first round global coordinates comfortably past that bound. Since
nand_s2 sits east of nand_m, the metal2 bus (next stage) has to
detour around nand_s2's own blob rather than through it -- see that
stage's own waypoints_um.
x_um=4.90 (not the 'place' stage's own 4.98) for the real 'a' pins
is this stub's own re-derivation: klayout.db against
sampler_nand2.gds shows the pin's own li1 pad at local x 4.665..5.085
but a SEPARATE, only-transitively-connected li1 strap (the mpb/mpa
gate strap the 'a' net is itself defined by) at local x 4.37..4.96 --
the two already overlap each other in the leaf cell's own composed
geometry, but 4.98 sits just east of the strap's own edge (a 0.02um
gap), so a wire starting there touches only the pad, not the strap,
and klt drc flags the near-miss as a li1.space.1 violation even
though every shape involved is the same 'a' net. 4.90 sits in both
the pad's and the strap's own ranges, so the new wire touches (and
merges with) both directly -- 0 violations. y_um=2.71 (not the
'place' stage's own 2.75, a value carried over from
layout/ro_ring5/cell.json's identical mpa/mnab placement for an
unrelated port) matches the real li1 pad's own centerline exactly.
The two stub segments below are two independent li1 rectangles, not
yet one net by JSON construction -- 'rst_n' becomes one net only
once the next stage bridges nand_m_a_ext to nand_s2_a_ext on
metal2; klt extract confirms physical connectivity from drawn
geometry, not from JSON net-name bookkeeping, so this is not a
correctness gap.

stages.name: rst_n_met1
_comment: A metal2 (met1) bus cannot cross either nand2 instance's own
footprint at y=2.71 -- that is exactly the met1 blob the previous
stage's li1 stubs route around, and vdd/vss's own met1 buses
already span the entire cell width at y=7.0/-3.5, so there is no
clear met1 lane at ANY height that both avoids the blobs and
avoids crossing vdd/vss's own vertical via stubs (tried and
rejected: climbing to y=6.0 to go over nand_s2 still crosses
nand_s2_vdd's own vertical stub at x=41.31, y 4.45..7.0). This
stage instead vias EACH stub tip independently, zero lateral
distance, straight up from li1 to met1 -- a single-hop via-drop,
identical in kind to every vdd/vss leg in 'route_supplies', just
with both ends at the same (x, y). The NEXT stage vias again,
met1 to met3 (also a single hop, the same hop 'ro_array_core's
own t2bridge stage uses), and runs the long haul entirely on
met3/'metal3' -- a plane no leaf cell in this assembly draws on at
all, so it is clear of every leaf's own internal congestion AND
of the met1 vdd/vss buses, without needing to dodge either.

stages.name: clk_met1
_comment: clk fan-out, step 1 of 2 (issue #22): via each of the five clk pins
straight up from li1 to met1, zero lateral distance -- the same
single-hop via-drop 'rst_n_met1' above uses, just five times.
design/sampler_core.spice's own gate assignments make clk a 5-pin
net: XMpc/XMnc's shared gate (inv_clk's input), XMtdp's gate
(tg_d's PMOS -> sampler_tg's 'ctrl'), XMfmn's gate (tg_fbm's NMOS
-> 'ctrlb'), XMtsn's gate (tg_s's NMOS -> 'ctrlb') and XMfsp's gate
(tg_fbs's PMOS -> 'ctrl'). The ctrl/ctrlb split ALTERNATES between
the four transmission gates (tg_d/tg_fbs take clk on ctrl, tg_fbm/
tg_s take it on ctrlb) because a master-slave DFF's feedback gates
run the opposite phase from their own stage's input gate -- which
is why no single 'clk above / clkb below' lane pair can serve both
nets, and why clk's own long haul (next stage) runs on met2 rather
than sharing a plane with clkb. See layout/sampler_dff/README.md.
Every one of the five pins is a real 0.42x0.42 li1 gate pad in its
own leaf cell (klayout.db against sampler_tg.gds: ctrl at local
own input strap is a dogbone with the IDENTICAL two pads joined by
a 0.17-wide bar). gen-compose's via-drop landing pad is a fixed
0.42 um square (_VIA_LANDING_SIZE_UM, independent of
routing.width_um), so it lands exactly on such a pad and merges
with it, adding no notch.
That fixed pad size is why inv_clk's clk port is declared here at
y=1.03 and NOT at the y=1.7 the 'place' stage uses for ro_buf's own
'a' port. y=1.7 is the middle of the dogbone's narrow 0.17-wide bar
(li1 x 0.46..0.63 there); y=1.03 is the centre of its own lower 0.42
pad, the same height as the two ctrlb pins this net also lands on.
BOTH were built and DRC'd, not just reasoned about, and BOTH are
clean -- the y=1.7 variant's concave step against the lower pad's
top edge measures 0.25 um, above sky130's own li1.space.1 (0.17 um),
so 'it would notch' is wrong; recorded here so it is not
re-derived. What y=1.7 costs is a 0.42-wide li1 pad dropped across a
0.17-wide bar directly over the inverter's gates -- extra
li1-over-poly on a clock net for no benefit. At y=1.03 the landing
pad is an EXACT overlay: inv_clk's li1 strap in the composed
sampler_dff.gds is polygon-for-polygon identical to ro_buf.gds's
own, adding no li1 at all, and the whole net's met1 geometry sits
on two heights only (1.03 and 2.5).
clk fan-out, step 2 of 2 (issue #22): one 5-pin bundle net whose
whole long haul runs on met2 ('metal3' role) in a single basement
lane at y=-1.70, with a vertical drop at each pin's own x and an
automatic met2->met1 via-drop onto the met1 pad the previous stage
put there. legs[] (klayout-tools #1529) names all four legs
explicitly so the spanning tree is the intended left-to-right
chain and every leg's path is steered through the lane, rather
than letting the nearest-first search pick default L-shapes.
waypoints_um is rejected outright on a >2-pin net, so legs[] is
the only way to steer a fan-out of this shape.
Why y=-1.70, and why met2 rather than met1:
- met1 is unusable for ANY horizontal haul across this cell.
The band it would need (-0.29 < y < 4.03, between the vss and
vdd buses' own merged met1 footprints) is blocked at BOTH
nand2 instances by that leaf's own internal met1 via stack
same obstruction 'rst_n_stub' above had to escape, here
spanning the full height of the usable band instead of just
part of it.
- met2 is drawn by no leaf cell in this assembly at all; before
this stage the only met2 in the whole composed cell is rst_n's
own bus at (13.79,2.50;45.11,2.92). A lane BELOW the device
rows keeps every clk leg clear of it by construction: the two
ctrlb drops (x=24.6 and x=29.74) are the only clk verticals
whose x falls inside rst_n's own span, and both stop at their
pin (y=1.03, met2 pad top 1.24), 1.26 um short of rst_n's own
lower edge. Routing clk ABOVE instead would short those two
verticals straight through rst_n's bus.
- y=-1.70 specifically: below every leaf's own drawn geometry
(the tallest southward reach is sampler_tg's psub tap at
y=-2.49) and above nothing it must clear on its own layer
(met2 is empty down here). The met1 vss bus underneath it
(y -3.585..-0.29) is a different layer and needs no clearance.
The lane spans x 0.545..49.03, so the cell bbox does not grow.
Reserved for clkb (next increment, NOT routed here): clkb's own
five pins are inv_clk's output plus the OPPOSITE gate of each
transmission gate -- tg_d.ctrlb (5.31,1.03), tg_fbm.ctrl
Because that assignment alternates against clk's, clkb cannot use
a second met2 lane on either side without crossing one of clk's
own five verticals. The corridor left for it is met1 at y ~ 0.40
-- clear of clk's own met1 pads (whose lowest edge is y=0.82,
0.335 um away, against sky130's 0.14 um met1.space.1) and of the
vss bus's own met1 (top edge y=-0.29) -- with a short met2 hop
over each of the two nand2 met1 blobs named above. Those two hops
sit at x 12..14 and x 43..45, where clk has no vertical at all.
